description:
AllpaOrbit: la tierra monitoreada desde el espacio 🌱🛰️

Hola, somos AllpaOrbit.  

El nombre resume nuestra idea: usar observaciones de la Tierra de la NASA para cuidar el suelo agrícola del Perú.
summary:
AllpaOrbit is a climate-smart agriculture platform designed to help farmers in the Majes Irrigation Project adapt to the growing impacts of climate change. Using NASA Earth observation data, including temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, and vegetation indicators, the platform transforms complex satellite information into practical tools such as climate alerts, irrigation recommendations, and crop monitoring insights.
The project addresses the Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge by enabling farmers to anticipate climate-related risks before they negatively affect crop productivity. In Majes, rising temperatures threaten agricultural production, with avocado yields potentially declining from 25 to less than 10 tons per hectare. This not only impacts crop yields but also increases pressure on water resources and farmers' incomes.
By providing actionable, data-driven recommendations, AllpaOrbit helps optimize water use, reduce uncertainty in agricultural decision-making, and strengthen farmers' resilience to climate change. Our goal is to transform space data into smarter decisions that protect crops, water resources, and rural livelihoods while promoting sustainable agriculture in Majes and other climate-vulnerable farming regions.
details:
ALLPA ORBIT - Plan Your Farming Season with NASA Data

WHAT DOES IT DO?

Allpa Orbit is a web application designed for small and medium-sized irrigated farmers in southern Peru. It starts with the Pampa de Majes (Arequipa), a desert agricultural region sustained by water from the Condoroma Reservoir in the upper Colca River basin.

Every growing season, farmers face the same question: What should I plant this year, in what sequence, and will I have enough water? Today, many farmers answer this by following what their neighbors plant. As a result, many choose the same crops, market prices fall at harvest time, and during dry years water shortages occur halfway through the season.

Allpa Orbit answers this question for the entire year. It combines NASA satellite observations with official data on crop prices, production costs, yields, and planting intentions. The information is presented in simple, farmer-friendly language while providing technical evidence for specialists and decision-makers.

HOW DOES IT WORK?

Step 1 - Your Farm

The farmer outlines the field boundaries on a satellite image and enters the farm size in hectares. The app automatically identifies the agricultural zone and retrieves the corresponding climate, water, and market information.

Step 2 - Satellite Analysis

Using NASA satellite imagery, the platform analyzes the field and calculates vegetation indicators such as NDVI. This helps determine cropping history, fallow periods, and nearby agricultural activity.

Step 3 - Water Availability

The app provides easy-to-understand information about:

  • Current water storage in the Condoroma Reservoir compared to historical averages.
  • Seasonal rainfall measured through NASA satellites.
  • The probability that the reservoir will refill during the current season.
  • Weekly weather forecasts and irrigation recommendations.

Step 4 - Crop Planning

Farmers define their usual crop rotation or select a preferred first crop. They can evaluate plans with two or three crop cycles per year.

Step 5 - Results

The platform compares the farmer’s plan with the best alternatives for the region, highlighting:

  • The most profitable option.
  • The option that uses the least water.
  • Expected net profit.
  • Financial risk.
  • Water sufficiency by month.
  • Oversupply alerts.
  • Local crop suitability.

BENEFITS

  • Plans the entire farming year rather than just the next crop.
  • Warns farmers in advance if water shortages are expected.
  • Identifies market oversupply risks before planting.
  • Displays net profit instead of gross revenue.
  • Translates complex information into clear and practical guidance.
  • Provides full transparency on data sources and evidence.

EXPECTED IMPACT

  • Fewer economic losses caused by poor planting decisions.
  • More efficient use of irrigation water in regions dependent on a single reservoir.
  • Greater resilience to climate variability and drought.
  • Improved agricultural planning through the integration of satellite and economic data.

TECHNOLOGIES USED

Backend

  • Python

Frontend

  • React
  • TypeScript
  • Vite

Testing

  • unittest
  • Vitest
  • Playwright

NASA Data Sources

  • NASA POWER
  • GPM IMERG
  • SWOT
  • HLS
  • MODIS
  • SMAP

Additional Data Sources

  • MIDAGRI
  • AUTODEMA
  • NOAA
  • FAO
  • ANA
  • SENAMHI
  • BCRP

Development Tools

  • Git
  • GitHub

WHAT MAKES IT INNOVATIVE?

  • Combines satellite, climate, water, and economic information into a single decision-support tool.
  • Shifts the focus from “What should I plant next?” to “What is the best annual crop rotation strategy?”
  • Detects oversupply risks before planting begins.
  • Presents information through three levels: simple summaries, detailed explanations, and technical evidence.

DESIGN PRINCIPLES

  • Never display invented or unsupported data.
  • Clearly distinguish between water availability, revenue, and net profit.
  • Validate models using historical observations.
  • Prioritize mobile-first design for farmers.
  • Remain operational even if a data source becomes temporarily unavailable.
  • Protect farmer privacy and communicate system limitations transparently.
